subject: Redwood MAP & Reservation: GPU pool sizing, term and burst policy for Acme AI
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@acme-ai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interest in Dedicated Reservation + MAP and evaluation timeline

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our CTO and infra leads liked the latency profiles. We’re ready to start putting together a mutual action plan so we can accelerate a production evaluation and then move to a reserved GPU pool if the eval hits our targets.

High level asks from our side:
- Short evaluation (2–3 week) with a representative traffic mix for cost/latency numbers
- A MAP that ties pricing/discounts to commits and ramp milestones
- Clear burst policy for traffic spikes during spikes in customer usage
- Guidance on GPU pool sizing (we expect sustained 100–200 RPS at 512 tokens)

Can you share a proposed MAP and a draft SOW with committed capacity, recommended pool size, term options, and sample pricing (including discount tiers tied to MAP milestones)? If we can get alignment this week, procurement can fast-track PO approvals.

Cheers,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme AI

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest in Dedicated Reservation + MAP and evaluation timeline

Emma — great to hear, and thanks for the clear asks. I’ve attached a first-pass MAP and draft SOW (Acme_MAP_Redwood_v1.pdf, SOW-draft-acme.docx) plus a quick capacity-sizing worksheet (capacity-sizing-sheet.csv). Key points up front:

Summary of proposed approach
- Evaluation: 2-week eval with a dedicated, short-term trial slice (non-reserved) to validate latency and token costs. We’ll provision a 4xA100-equivalent pool during eval for representative load.
- MAP milestones and commercial tie-ins:
  * Milestone 1 (Eval complete, week 2): Performance acceptance test passed — Redwood issues a 10% one-time credit toward first invoice.
  * Milestone 2 (Commit signed, within 30 days of Eval): Customer commits to a 12-month reservation for the agreed pool size — pricing tier A applied (baseline unit $/GPU-hr).
  * Milestone 3 (90-day ramp target): If average sustained util reaches ≥70% by month 3, additional 5% discount applied for months 4–12.
- Term options: 12 / 24 month terms; 24 months gives extra 7% on top of MAP discounts.
- Burst policy: All reserved pools include a baseline burst allowance (up to 25% over committed throughput for short windows). For sustained bursts we offer paid burst capacity from a shared burst pool (pre-warmed) billed at a lower overage rate than on-demand. Details in the SOW section 3.2.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick scoping call (30 min) today or tomorrow with Vivek to confirm sizing and target RPS distribution.
2) We’ll update the MAP with any sizing changes and issue a redline-friendly SOW.
3) If Acme accepts baseline terms, we’ll provision the eval environment within 48 hours of PO.

I’m copying Vivek for the sizing call — Vivek, would 3pm PT today work to review the CSV?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0123

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest in Dedicated Reservation + MAP and evaluation timeline

Emma / Neha — moving to sizing specifics. I reviewed Acme’s traffic notes in the CSV and sketched two options:

Sizing options (rough)
- Option A (conservative): 4xA100-equivalent nodes (baseline): expected sustained 120 RPS @ 512 tokens, headroom for short spikes; estimated baseline latency p50 70–90ms depending on prompt mixing.
- Option B (aggressive): 8xA100-equivalent nodes: handles sustained 220 RPS, better headroom for KV/cache reuse and larger batch efficiencies.

Commercial implications
- 4-node pool (12-month): baseline monthly commit = $XX,XXX; 10% MAP credit after eval; burst allowance up to 25% for 30-minute windows; overage billed at 1.5x baseline unit rate.
- 8-node pool (12-month): baseline monthly commit = $YY,YYY; better unit economics (~12% lower $/token) once sustained util >65%; burst allowance up to 20% (we recommend higher baseline to reduce burst use).

Operational notes
- During the eval we can enable prefix KV caching and continuous batching to reflect production performance. We’ll provide a short runbook for traffic shaping during the evaluation.
- If Acme needs guaranteed burst above the default allowance, we can reserve a small pre-warmed burst pool (priced in the SOW) — recommended only if you expect >30% spikes regularly.

I’ll be on the call at 3pm PT — we can walk the CSV and update numbers live.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Mendes <carlos@acme-ai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma@acme-ai.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest in Dedicated Reservation + MAP and evaluation timeline

Thanks — call was helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before procurement will accept a PO:
1) Burst semantics: how is "25% for 30 minutes" enforced and measured? Do we get alerting and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if burst capacity is exhausted?
2) Discount timing: you mentioned a 10% credit after eval and an additional 5% after 90-day ramp. Are these applied pro-rata on the next invoice or as line-item credits? We need clarity to show savings in our TCO model.
3) Early termination / term flexibility: procurement wants a 90-day exit window in case production shows persistent regressions (we'd accept fee if blackout). Is that something Redwood will consider for a 12-month commit?

Also, we are willing to accelerate signature if Redwood can include a milestone-driven early close discount: if Redwood commits to provisioning the reserved pool within 48 hours of PO and we sign within 7 days of the MAP agreement, Acme will accept a 5% higher commit volume (i.e. move from 4->6 nodes) but requests a stepped discount: 12-month term: 12% discount if signed within 7 days, else 10%.

Carlos
VP Product Operations, Acme AI

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendes <carlos@acme-ai.com>, Emma Li <emma@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest in Dedicated Reservation + MAP and evaluation timeline

Carlos — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and a proposed commercial redline to include in the MAP / SOW: 

1) Burst semantics and enforcement
- Measurement: Burst is measured at the pool throughput level in 1-minute granularity with a rolling 30-minute window. If aggregated throughput exceeds baseline + 25% allowance for more than the configured window, additional requests draw from the shared burst pool or are billed as overage. We’ll provide dashboards and Slack alerts for 80%/95% thresholds.
- Fallback: We support automatic routing to a compatible, lower-cost model variant as a graceful degradation path; this is configurable per-route in the SOW.

2) Discount timing and crediting
- Eval credit (10%): issued as a line-item credit on the first invoice after eval completion.
- Ramp discount (5%): applied pro-rata starting the month after the 90-day check; we’ll include a short audit clause to validate utilization.
- Early-close incentive (Acme suggestion): we can offer 12% off baseline unit rate if signed and PO issued within 7 days of MAP acceptance and Redwood provisions reserved pool within 48 hours of PO. Otherwise standard 10% apply.

3) Early termination
- For 12-month contracts we can add a limited exit clause: after an initial 90-day production acceptance window, Acme may terminate with a 45-day notice and a termination fee equal to 2 months of committed spend (capped). This is a redline we can add to the SOW.

Action items
- I’ll update the MAP and SOW to incorporate the burst enforcement language, discount timing, and the proposed early termination clause then share for redlines (attached).
- If you confirm the early-close target and timeframe, I’ll ask legal to prepare a DB-approved redline for signature and we’ll reserve the burst pool capacity during the signature window.

If this looks good I’ll circulate the updated doc by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Acme_MAP_Redwood_v1.pdf (updated), SOW-draft-acme.docx (redline-ready)
